caption: The drawing depicts a sampler-style needlework design on a beige or light tan background, bordered by a repeating green and yellow vine motif. The composition contains various embroidered objects, including several floral arrangements in vases, two pairs of yellow-breasted birds facing each other on branches, large flowers, small trees, hexagonal patterns, and multiple geometric shapes. In the upper center is an inscription bordered by an octagonal leafy frame, reading, "May truth direct my heart and voice, And virtue be my only choice; Sweet innocence my life attend, And constantly from vice defend." The upper left section has the names "Joseph Wilson" and "Ann Wilson," while the upper right section has the initials "EW AW MW JW" and "Mary Wilson." The central lower section includes the name "Sidney Wilson" and the year "Work 1821" surrounded by a wreath. The lower green band indicates a grassy area with more floral arrangements and stylized geometric containers. In the corner of the image, there is a rectangular inset showing a detail at "actual size," featuring an embroidered plant with green leaves and two ripe strawberries. The colors throughout the drawing are mainly greens, reds, yellows, pinks, and browns. The artist's name, "A. Walbeck," appears on the lower right, and the annotation "2/3 actual size" is written below the main needlework reproduction.
title: Sampler
cluster: #01 — Textile Arts: Quilts, Samplers, and Embroideries
